newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Elektrowatt up on rumours of stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Elektrowatt up on rumours of stake sale.

text.p: Shares in Swiss industrial and power group Elektrowatt AG soared on Friday on renewed speculation that banking group CS Holding had found a buyer or buyers for its 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt.
Elektrowatt bearer shares were 12 francs or 2.3 percent higher at 522 Swiss francs at 1400 GMT, as opposed to a rise of 0.4 percent in the blue-ship Swiss Market Index (SMI) to around 3,900 points.
Elektrowatt said it planned to release a statement at 4:00 p.m. (1500 GMT) -- half an hour before the Swiss Exchange closes.
Traders said this would be an unusual time to to announce any major changes because it would be during active trading.
Elektrowatt earlier on Friday hit a year's high of 523 Swiss francs.

CS Holding declined to comment on market rumours that it would finally carry out long-standing intentions to sell its Elektrowatt stake as part of a concentration on core banking and financial business.
"These are all rumours and we do not comment on rumours," a CS Holding spokesman said.

An Elektrowatt spokesman, queried by Reuters about market rumours of a news conference, said no news conference was planned. "I can confirm that we will release a media statement at 4:00 p.m.," he said.
Speculation on Elektrowatt is closely linked to rumours around utility and industrial holding Motor-Columbus, which is majority owned by Union Bank of Swizterland.

Like CS Holding, UBS wants to dispose of non-bank holdings and has long talked about selling its 76 percent stake in Motor-Columbus, whose main asset is a 56 percent holding in Swiss power utility Atel.
Traders have repeatedly speculated that Elektrowatt's energy business would somehow be merged with Motor-Columbus to form some kind of Swiss energy holding company.
But in response to today's speculation, Motor-Columbus said it planned no statements today.
"We will not put out anything," executive board member Rita Dreier told Reuters when asked if any statement was planned.
UBS was also not planning to make any statements today, a spokesman said.
Motor-Columbus shares at 1400 were 20 Swiss francs higher at 2,740, a gain of 0.7 percent, after reaching a year's high of 2,775 earlier in the day.
